title: finding(gate): the two document-count pins have no in-file positive control — both assert [] against an empty header, so a deleted pattern would still pass
body:
Found while carrying objectui#7448's document-count pin from its third copy onto the two twins (objectui#7888). Measured, not inferred.

## What

`scripts/__tests__/check-links-workflow.test.ts` carries the pin **and** an in-file positive control beside it: a second test that fixtures the pin's reach in both directions — 6 shapes it must fire on, 10 numbers a header may legitimately keep. Its docstring names the negative that decides the bound (`~297 site-absolute links`, the near miss that sets the two-word limit).

The two twins — `scripts/__tests__/check-doc-fence-languages.test.ts` and `scripts/__tests__/check-doc-component-types.test.ts` — now carry the same pattern and **no fixture at all**. Each pin has exactly one assertion, and that assertion reads a workflow header that is empty today. So on today's tree both pins assert `[] toEqual []`: they pass, and they would pass identically if the pattern were deleted, reversed, or narrowed back to adjacency.

## Why it matters

That is the failure mode the third copy's own docstring cites by name:

> A pin that cannot fail is not a pin, and this repository has shipped one with zero demonstrated power before (objectui#7466: 0/32 on the broken tree AND 0/32 on the fixed one).

Two concrete things went unnoticed for exactly this reason:

- the adjacency narrowness itself (objectui#7888) — the twins shipped a pattern that missed `15 INTERNAL documents` while their docstrings claimed to catch it, and nothing in either file exercised the claim;
- a **false positive** in the old pattern, found only by running it by hand: on the string `#7448 documents the rule`, the pre-objectui#7888 twin pattern returned `["7448 documents"]`. An issue reference directly followed by a population noun read as a document count. No test in either file would have caught that either.

The power of the widened pattern was demonstrated on objectui#7888 by a four-direction ablation run out of band (inject the missed shape, restore, inject a number that is correct today, inject an issue reference). That measurement lives in a PR description; nothing in the repository holds it.

## The shape that already exists

`check-links-workflow.test.ts`'s second `it(...)` block, verbatim in structure: a `rotted` array asserted `not.toEqual([])` and a `legitimate` array asserted `toEqual([])`. The fixtures are already written and already reviewed there. This is a copy of a landed control into two files, not a new design.

Note the twins' pin reads only its workflow header, so the fixture arrays exercise the pattern directly rather than through a file read — the same way the third copy does.

## Not this card

Coverage of the pins (which surfaces they read) is objectui#7901. This is about the pins' demonstrated power on the surface they already read, and the two are independent.

Back-links: objectui#7448, objectui#7825, objectui#7885, objectui#7888, objectui#7901.
